rubric.title: Cinematography
rubric.goal: Evaluate whether the video correctly uses cinematic techniques that match the elegant, refined lab-to-lifestyle reveal narrative and makes the bottle the final hero.
criteria: Shot design follows a clear progression: establishing tabletop/product layout → action close-up (pump onto card) → proof moment (UV lamp color contrast) → lifestyle cue (sunglasses slide in) → hero hold (bottle in sharp focus).
Camera movement is controlled and premium (e.g., subtle dolly/push-in during proof or hero shot), avoiding handheld shakiness unless intentionally minimal and stabilized.
Framing emphasizes the key entities without clutter: bottle and card are readable; pump nozzle and dispensed line are clearly visible; UV lamp is shown enough to establish causality.
Macro/close-up coverage is used appropriately for the sunscreen line and bead color change; focus pulls are deliberate (e.g., from card contrast back to bottle hero).
Lighting is clean, soft, and high-key/neutral to feel clinical yet refined; reflections on bottle and sunglasses are controlled (no harsh specular blowouts).
Color grading supports 'elegant, refined' with neutral whites and light grays; purple UV-bead reaction is vivid but not neon-clipped or artifacted.
Pacing and transitions are smooth and product-ad-like: no abrupt jump cuts that break comprehension; proof moment is held long enough to read the contrast; final linger feels intentional.
Depth of field is used to guide attention: background falls off subtly; final hero shot keeps bottle tack-sharp while other elements are tastefully softened.
Continuity of screen direction and object placement is maintained across cuts (bottle/card/sunglasses positions remain coherent).
The final composition clearly crowns the pump bottle as the hero (center or rule-of-thirds emphasis, clean negative space, minimal distractions).

Composition and framing that support the emotional tone
Lighting and color grading that enhance the mood
Shot transitions and pacing that fit the storytelling
Visual style consistency with the intended atmosphere

rubric.title: Physics adherence
rubric.goal: Evaluate whether all interactions, actions, and state changes (pumping sunscreen, card tilting, UV-bead color change, sliding sunglasses) follow normal physical phenomena and cause-and-effect.

Sunscreen consistency is believable for mineral sunscreen (viscous lotion/cream): forms a line on the card with realistic thickness, slight spreading, and no impossible levitation or instant drying unless implied.
Contact and adhesion are correct: sunscreen line sticks to the card surface; no hovering gap; edges behave like a viscous material.
Presenter hand-object interactions are physically correct: fingers grip the card naturally; card rotates around the hand grip; no finger warping or slipping through objects.

Card tilt under UV lamp follows gravity and torque: smooth rotation; the sunscreen line may sag minimally if very thick/tilted steeply but should not slide unrealistically or remain unaffected by extreme angles.
UV lamp is positioned plausibly relative to the card: illumination direction is consistent; shadows and highlights respond accordingly.

UV-bead reaction is temporally and spatially plausible: untreated area turns purple after exposure (not before); treated strip remains pale; boundary aligns with where sunscreen was applied without drifting or flickering.
Color change progresses consistently (e.g., gradual shift or quick reaction) but without random patching, crawling artifacts, or reversion while still under UV.
Sunglasses slide motion obeys friction: initial push by presenter, then deceleration to a stop; no sudden speed jumps, floating, or clipping through the tabletop/bottle.
Object stability: bottle remains stationary unless touched; no wobble without cause; tabletop provides consistent support (no sinking, skating, or scale shifts).

Natural state changes (material deformation, color-change behavior)

criteria: Are the dancers’ slow arm circles continuous and evenly paced (no stutter, frame skipping, or sudden limb pops)?
Does the acceleration into heel stamps feel like a smooth tempo increase rather than abrupt speed jumps or inconsistent cadence?
Are the two dancers tightly synchronized in timing and amplitude (mirrored arm paths, matching stamp cadence), without drift or desynchronization artifacts?
During the crossing behind the violinist, do trajectories remain smooth with continuous walking/stepping motion (no teleporting, foot sliding, or jitter at occlusion boundaries)?
Do fountain jets rise higher in a smooth, rhythmic manner (no flickering heights, popping columns, or unstable water patterns between frames)?
Is the violinist’s posture stable and movement (if any bowing) smooth, without micro-jitter or warping?
Is the final identical mirrored pose held steadily with minimal wobble and no sudden re-positioning, clearly establishing new opposite sides?
focus_points: Smooth, continuous body motion (arms, torso, feet)
Natural execution without stuttering or jittering
Fluid transitions between motion states (slow arm circles -> fast stamps -> crossing -> final pose)
Realistic timing and speed (acceleration curve, synchronized cadence)
Stable temporal coherence for fountain jets and occlusions

anchors.1: Severe motion artifacts throughout: heavy jitter, freezing, teleporting, limb popping, or unusable synchronization; fountain motion flickers wildly.
anchors.2: Noticeable irregularities in key actions: arm circles stutter, stamping cadence inconsistent, crossing contains jumps/clipping, or jet height changes flicker/popup.
anchors.3: Generally smooth but with occasional hiccups: minor jitter, slight desync, small speed inconsistencies, or brief fountain flicker that does not fully break comprehension.
anchors.4: Smooth and natural overall: synchronization reads well, acceleration feels coherent, crossing is clean with rare minor artifacts.
anchors.5: Exceptionally smooth: all movements are fluid and temporally consistent; synchronization is tight; crossing and final pose are stable; fountain jets animate rhythmically without flicker.

rubric.title: Physics adherence
rubric.goal: Evaluate whether all actions and causal effects (heel stamps, crossing, fountain jet response) follow plausible real-world physics and timing.
criteria: Do heel stamps show plausible foot-ground contact (no foot sliding through stone, no floating, correct weight transfer, realistic recoil)?
Do dancers’ garments, hair, and limbs move with believable inertia and joint limits during arm circles and rapid stamping (no rubbery deformation or impossible bends)?
Is the sound-implied ‘echo against stone’ supported visually by realistic stamping force cues (posture bracing, slight body impact response), even if audio is absent?
Does the fountain water behave realistically (gravity-driven arcs/columns, splash patterns, continuous flow) without unnatural clumping, reverse-falling, or instant teleporting jets?
Is the causal link plausible: as stamping intensifies, jets rise higher with a reasonable response latency and smooth pressure change (not frame-instant height jumps unrelated to rhythm)?
During the side-switch, do dancers pass behind the violinist with correct occlusion (who blocks whom), no body intersections, and consistent depth ordering?
Are positions consistent over time (no sudden position pops), especially at the moment they cross and when they end on new opposite sides?
focus_points: Physical plausibility of contacts and collisions (feet with stone, dancers passing each other/behind violinist)
Realistic cause-and-effect (stamp intensity linked to jet height changes)
Natural material behavior (water flow, fabric motion, hair motion)
Temporal consistency of physical processes (jet ramp-up/down, momentum in dance)
Absence of impossible phenomena (phasing, anti-gravity, disjointed limb physics)

anchors.1: Severe physics violations: floating bodies, feet not contacting ground, water behaving impossibly (levitating, reversing), frequent phasing/intersections, or nonsensical jet response.
anchors.2: Major physical errors in key moments: stamping contact wrong, crossing causes clipping/teleporting, fountain jets jump discontinuously or behave non-fluidly, obvious joint/cloth physics failures.
anchors.3: Mostly plausible with noticeable minor issues: occasional foot sliding, slight limb warping, small water artifacts, or mildly abrupt jet-height changes but overall understandable.
anchors.4: Good realism: convincing footwork contacts and crossing occlusions; fountain behavior and jet-height changes feel physically coherent with only rare minor artifacts.
anchors.5: Highly realistic: all dance contacts, body mechanics, occlusions, and fountain fluid dynamics are consistent and natural; jet height increases smoothly and rhythmically with plausible response timing.

rubric.title: Cinematography
rubric.goal: Evaluate cinematic techniques matching the emotional tone and narrative purpose
criteria: Establishing shot clearly communicates a calm early-autumn wetland boardwalk before the cold front (readable setting, season cues, quiet tone).
Camera language supports a neutral, balanced mood (no horror-style dutch angles, no overly frantic handheld unless motivated by the gust event).
Composition consistently frames key entities: boardwalk planks in foreground/leading lines; reed-lined water visible; birder (navy jacket) and child readable; geese visible resting before takeoff.
Shot progression matches narrative beats: calm observation -> cold front arrives -> reeds/water intensify -> geese take off across frame -> leaves swirl along planks.
Camera movement motivates attention: gentle pan/slow push during calm; slight increase in dynamism when wind hits; tracks geese takeoff without losing spatial context.
Lens choice and depth of field help clarity: enough DOF to keep subject interactions readable (birder/child + geese) without excessive background blur that hides reeds/water behavior.
Lighting and color grading convey early autumn and approaching cold front (cooler shift, slightly desaturated/steelier tones during front) while maintaining natural realism.
Exposure/contrast preserve detail in reeds, water ripples, and flying geese (no blown highlights on water, no crushed blacks on clothing).
Transitions and pacing are smooth and story-appropriate (no random jump cuts; event escalation feels natural; timing allows viewer to register geese resting before takeoff).
Spatial continuity is maintained (consistent screen direction for geese crossing; boardwalk orientation stable; no unexplained teleporting viewpoints).
Wind arrival is cinematically communicated (audience can infer change via visible reed bend + water texture shift; optional subtle camera shake only if consistent and restrained).
Visual style remains consistent across the clip (no sudden changes in art style, color palette, or rendering quality between calm and windy segments).

anchors.1: Cinematic techniques contradict the prompt (chaotic or mismatched tone; key subjects not framed; lighting/grade wrong for wetland/autumn; incoherent pacing).
anchors.2: Major cinematic issues: poor framing of birder/child/geese; unclear boardwalk/wetland context; abrupt or confusing transitions; lighting/grade inconsistent with early autumn/cold front.
anchors.3: Adequate coverage of the scene and events, but cinematic choices are generic or uneven (some missed beats, mild continuity problems, or mood not clearly neutral/balanced).
anchors.4: Strong cinematic execution: clear story beats and readable compositions; good mood and lighting with minor issues (small continuity slips, slightly off pacing, or occasional suboptimal framing).
anchors.5: Excellent cinematic storytelling: calm-to-front escalation is visually and emotionally coherent; compositions consistently highlight entities/actions; lighting/grade and camera work feel intentionally matched to the narrative.

rubric.title: Motion smoothness
rubric.goal: Evaluate the naturalness and fluidity of all motions and interactions
criteria: Birder holding binoculars is stable and continuous (no hand jitter, snapping arm poses, or binocular deformation/frame-to-frame drift).
Child pointing gesture is smooth with consistent limb anatomy and continuous motion (no popping elbows/fingers or pose resets).
Wind-driven reed motion is continuous and coherent over time (no staccato bending, looping glitches, or synchronized 'wave' artifacts across all reeds).
Water ripple evolution is temporally smooth (no texture crawling, tiling jumps, or sudden pattern resets when wind increases).
Geese takeoff is fluid: wingbeats cycle smoothly; acceleration is continuous; no frame skipping, teleporting, or shape morphing of birds mid-flight.
Flock movement across the frame maintains stable trajectories and speed changes (no sudden direction flips, jittery spacing changes, or individuals blinking in/out).
Leaf swirl and skitter is continuous: leaves follow smooth arcs and sliding paths along planks without jitter, freezing, or unnatural speed spikes.
Camera motion (if any) is smooth and stabilized appropriately for the neutral tone (no unintended shake, rolling shutter wobble, or abrupt pans).
Transitions between calm and windy states occur smoothly (wind intensity ramps plausibly rather than hard-cutting multiple times).
No temporal artifacts: ghosting, motion smear inconsistent with shutter, duplicated frames, or discontinuous shadows indicating frame interpolation failures.
focus_points: Natural execution of key actions (pointing, holding, takeoff)

anchors.1: Motion is severely broken: frequent stutter, jitter, freezing, teleportation, or morphing across most entities.
anchors.2: Noticeable motion problems in key actions (geese takeoff, leaf swirl, or reed/water motion) with repeated discontinuities.
anchors.3: Generally watchable motion with occasional glitches (minor jitter in reeds/water, some bird wingbeat inconsistency, brief frame hiccups).
anchors.4: Smooth and natural overall; only rare minor artifacts that do not distract from the narrative.
anchors.5: Exceptionally smooth motion: all character gestures, wind/water dynamics, flock flight, and leaf skitter are fluid, continuous, and temporally consistent.

rubric.title: Physics adherence
rubric.goal: Evaluate whether all interactions and state changes follow natural physical laws
criteria: Wind effects on reeds are physically plausible: reeds bend with a coherent wind direction, show elastic response, and vary naturally (not all reeds moving identically).
Water behavior matches strong wind: ripples align with wind direction, increase in amplitude/frequency after the cold front arrives, and remain temporally consistent.

Cold front arrival is represented as a state change that plausibly increases wind intensity rather than instantaneous impossible transformations (no sudden water freezing, teleporting fog walls, etc.).
Geese resting on water behave plausibly (buoyancy, spacing, gentle bobbing) before takeoff.
Goose takeoff mechanics are credible: wingbeats generate lift; bodies accelerate forward/up; feet contact water during the start is plausible; no hovering or unnatural instantaneous acceleration.
Flock motion is coherent: individuals maintain plausible separation, avoid interpenetration, and follow consistent heading across the frame.
Interaction between wing rush and fallen leaves is plausible: leaves lift/spiral due to gust and turbulence, then skitter along boardwalk with friction and intermittent hops.
Leaves follow realistic trajectories: no sharp right-angle turns without force; no levitation; speed changes correspond to gust strength and surface friction.
Boardwalk planks are rigid and stationary; leaves slide on top without phasing into the wood; no clipping through the boardwalk surface.

Causal chain is respected: wind intensifies -> reeds bend & water ripples hard -> geese take off -> resulting air disturbance contributes to leaf swirl (not leaves swirling before any wind/wing event).
Temporal consistency: once wind strengthens, reeds/water do not suddenly revert to calm without cause; geese do not revert to resting mid-flight.
No physically impossible artifacts: objects phasing, scale popping, reversed gravity, inconsistent shadows that suggest impossible light-object interactions.
focus_points: Realistic material behavior (reeds, water, leaves, birds)

anchors.1: Severe physics violations throughout (floating/teleporting birds or leaves, water behaving like cloth/solid, reeds bending impossibly, pervasive clipping).
anchors.2: Major physical errors in key events (unrealistic goose takeoff, wind effects inconsistent, leaves moving against forces, frequent interpenetration).
anchors.3: Mostly plausible with noticeable minor-to-moderate issues (some leaf trajectories off, occasional bird clipping, simplified water/reed dynamics).
anchors.4: Largely physically convincing; only rare minor implausibilities that do not break the causal chain (small timing or turbulence simplifications).
anchors.5: Highly realistic physics: wind-water-reed response, geese takeoff biomechanics, and wing-triggered leaf swirl all behave naturally with consistent cause-and-effect and no artifacts.
